title: Mixed-income rebalance - core vs project fragmentation
provenance: Emma, The Paper Birds (evidence log, 31 May 2026): part-time fundraiser; mix of grants, partnerships, commissioned work; core-vs-project balance 'feels fragmented'; the time sink is managing the process, not finding. Capacity relief is the value, not more options.

constraints.text: Secured income is almost all project-restricted; core costs are the recurring squeeze.

synthetic.title: Resilient organisations fund
synthetic.description: Unrestricted grants of £15,000-£40,000 per year over two years for established arts organisations. Explicitly for core costs.

funder_brief.what_they_fund: Unrestricted core funding for established arts organisations.
funder_brief.who_can_apply: Arts organisations with five or more years of history and income between £100,000 and £1 million.
funder_brief.decision_timeline: One round per year; decisions by December.

what_they_fund.snippet: grants are unrestricted and intended to support core organisational costs

expected.judge_guidance: The constraint to lead with is the restricted/unrestricted imbalance (the user's own note), not the headline gap. A 5 names it, points the recommendation set at core-cost/unrestricted routes (the Keystone fixture is planted; Esmée if pinned), and keeps total asks small - this user is part-time and the brief's load-reduction warning applies doubly. The mix flag should reflect the contract-heavy target vs grant-heavy reality, marked as judgment where it goes beyond the arithmetic. A response that ignores the existing pipeline (e.g. recommends things colliding with the 31 July commission deadline) loses R2/R7 credit. Note max_recommendations is tightened to 4 for this case: proportionality to a part-time fundraiser's capacity IS the test.

notes: Validates mix-vs-plan reasoning against the segment-3 pattern (coordination pain, not discovery pain). The tightened recommendation cap is deliberate and case-specific.
